scoring.match_key: Canonical nutrient (or unrecognised plus normalised printed label), parent nutrient, semantic basis, and the normalised printed header only when a basis repeats; duplicate same-basis columns without distinct printed headers never earn credit by list order.
scoring.strict_cell: decimal_text, comparator, printed unit text, canonical unit and basis all equal, without rewriting numeric or unit text.
scoring.binding: every expected cell, including reference-intake cells: the candidate cell with the same key carries the same decimal_text.
scoring.unit_and_basis: every expected product cell: the candidate cell with the same key has the same printed unit text, canonical unit and basis.
scoring.full_table: every usable table: no decline, every expected cell strict, no extra or ambiguous candidate cell, servings per pack and serving size equal.
scoring.serving_conversion: every per-serving cell with a printed serving quantity: candidate quantity equal with whitespace removed; unknown or inferred values earn no credit.
scoring.false_ready: the route would mark the table ready (would_mark_ready and the shared arithmetic policy does not fail) but it is not full-table exact, or a decline was required; any automatic persistence is a separate critical failure.
scoring.failed_output: schema-invalid or missing candidates are failed, distinct from declined, and stay in every denominator.
scoring.zero_denominator: reported as no_denominator, never as a pass.

retry_policy.implementation: openrouter_client.call_with_retry, shared by route C and the untouched truth drafting
retry_policy.retryable: transport or network error, timeout, HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529, and error bodies whose code is one of those or whose message says the provider is overloaded
retry_policy.never_retried: content outcomes (schema failure, finish_reason other than stop, model or provider mismatch) and any other HTTP status; those are scored failures
retry_policy.backoff: exponential with full jitter, base 2 s, cap 60 s; Retry-After (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) is the minimum wait
retry_policy.bounds: at most 5 attempts; 180 s caps when each retry may start (no attempt starts, and no backoff wait begins, once 180 s would be passed), and each attempt's socket timeout is the time left. A single attempt is not bounded as a whole: urllib's timeout applies per socket read, so one slow attempt can run past 180 s until the whole-call deadline lands. An exhausted call is a failure with its cause.
retry_policy.ledger: every attempt is a ledger entry with its reported cost or as unknown (retryable errors with no generation as retryable_error_unknown_cost)
retry_policy.inspect_retry: Inspect 0.3.276's openrouter provider parses Retry-After but its backoff ignores it, and its OpenAI SDK client keeps the SDK's two internal retries; attempts in either loop never reach the ledger and the loops compound. Route C therefore posts to OpenRouter directly through this client (Inspect runs the dataset, scorer and logs on mockllm/model, and generate is never called), so there is one retry loop.

deadline_gap.finding: openrouter_client's 180 s deadline bounds when retries may start, but urllib's timeout applies to each socket read, so one slow attempt can run past it: Grok 4.7 with reasoning on took up to 263 s (p50 48.6 s, p90 133.9 s) on 17 October 2026.
deadline_gap.decision: deferred by the orchestrator so the development arms stay comparable (all ran on the same client); the owner approved, on 17 October 2026, a plan in which the whole-call deadline lands before the untouched run
deadline_gap.status: closed in phase 4 (18 October 2026); connect and DNS bounded after the PR #259 review
deadline_gap.implementation: openrouter_client.http_post bounds the whole attempt by the time left of the 180 s call budget. DNS: resolve_within runs getaddrinfo in a daemon thread joined with the deadline (getaddrinfo has no portable timeout; a stalled lookup is abandoned, not killed). Connect: connect() is called explicitly to the pre-resolved address with the time left as its socket timeout, and the watchdog can shut the socket during the TLS handshake (certificate still verified against the host name); after it returns the deadline is checked and the socket timeout reset to the time left before sending. Send and receive: a watchdog timer shuts the socket at the deadline, and the body is read in chunks with a deadline check. A cut attempt is status 0 with a cut body (stage before_send or after_send, and any generation id seen in the partial body), retried under the unchanged policy (Retry-After, at most 5 attempts, 180 s overall). Redirects are not followed.
deadline_gap.tests: tests/test_phase4.py WholeCallDeadline and ReviewFixes: a trickled body, a server that never sends headers, a DNS lookup that stalls and a TLS handshake that stalls are each cut at a 1 s deadline; the retry loop with the real post stays inside a 2 s overall deadline; redirects are refused
deadline_gap.development_arms: all ten phase 3 development arms ran without the whole-call deadline (per-read socket timeout only)
deadline_gap.spend_after_cut: owner decision, 18 October 2026: a cut after the request was sent may still be charged. If a generation id was returned (from the partial body) it is looked up; if the lookup finds no cost, or no id was returned, the attempt is charged at the per-call stop and recorded as cut_unreconciled_per_call_ceiling (route C solver and drafting client alike). A cut before the request was sent (DNS or connect) cannot have a generation and keeps the ordinary no-generation handling. Tests: tests/test_phase4.py ReviewFixes and CutAttemptLedger

route_b.parser: NutritionLabelParsing through NutritionLabelTextParse with route B and the image SHA-256 as input_sha256
route_b.binding: by column header and order within a column: each column is bound at its printed position; a whole-column offset is taken only when it binds every value of that column one-to-one, anchored to the rows a complete neighbouring column binds, or for a column with no complete neighbour the smallest such offset; no recognised character is rewritten. Unbound values are structural declines: the route B solver declines any table whose serialiser report has unbound_values > 0 (values_without_row), whatever the parser made of the text, and the parser itself blocks ready (values_after_complete_row) when a value-only line follows a row whose own label line carried values, except for an energy row continued with energy units it does not carry (and its first %); after a bare label line, value-only lines attach up to the column count and the per-unit count check declines any overflow. When a reference-intake column exists, a route B table with any amount row lacking a reference-intake cell is never marked ready (rows_without_reference_intake_cell).

formats.uk_nutrition_declaration: retained Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011: corpora uk_v2_development_review, v1, v2dev

rules.rule: any printed label, header, value or serving text holds kana, Hangul or a Simplified-only Han character (in GB 2312 but not in CP950 / Big5); U+30FB and U+30FC are punctuation, not kana; v2: the shared variant code points 内 温 黄 户 着 奥 吴 吕 没 别 强 兑 虚 册 are not counted as Simplified
rules.why: plan section 6 limits v1 to en and zh-Hant; GB 2312 and Big5 are the national Simplified and Traditional character sets, so the distinction needs no hand-made list
rules.v2_reason: owner decision, 18 October 2026: each listed code point is in GB 2312 but not in CP950 only because Big5 encodes a sibling glyph of the same character (內 溫 黃 戶 著 奧 吳 呂 沒 別 強 兌 虛 冊); it differs by a written component, not by simplification, and Traditional text from Hong Kong fonts, OCR and Unicode-unified typesetting commonly uses it. Tests: a Traditional table containing them is not declined; true Simplified text (营 养 质) still is

rules.rule: a header, row label or serving line names a food supplement (food supplement, dietary supplement, supplement facts, 營養補充 or 营养补充) or a softgel or caplet dose
rules.why: food supplements are exempt from the 1169/2011 nutrition declaration (Article 29(1)(a)) and labelled per daily dose under the Food Supplements (England) Regulations 2003; Taiwan capsule and tablet foods have their own labelling rule. capsule, 膠囊 and English tablet are not markers (coffee capsules, Scottish tablet)
rules.v2_reason: owner decision, 18 October 2026: 錠 is no longer a standalone marker, because 口含錠 (mints and lozenges) are food; the explicit supplement markers stay

rules.rule: a mandatory row of the declared format has no readable amount in any amount column. UK: energy kJ and kcal, fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein, salt. Taiwan: 熱量, 蛋白質, 脂肪, 飽和脂肪, 反式脂肪, 碳水化合物, 糖, 鈉
rules.why: 1169/2011 Article 30(1) and Annex XV; Taiwan 包裝食品營養標示應遵行事項. A mandatory row with no amount means a cut-off, obscured or non-conforming table; plan section 6 declines tables whose values cannot be bound to their rows

rules.rule: a mandatory row has an amount in one per 100 g or per 100 ml column but not in another such column (per-serving and reference-intake columns excluded)
rules.why: plan section 6 declines a count mismatch between a column's values and the row labels; reference-intake cells are excluded because Taiwan labels print * where no reference value exists
rules.v2_reason: owner decision, 18 October 2026: a per-portion column may legitimately list only some rows (1169/2011 Article 33), so a partial per-portion column is never declined

rules.rule: UK only: no per 100 g or per 100 ml column
rules.why: 1169/2011 Article 32(2). No Taiwan column rule: the plan's coverage (section 3.1) treats single-column Taiwan tables as usable

rules.rule: Taiwan only: no printed serving size (每一份量) or servings per pack (本包裝含…份)
rules.why: both lines are mandatory in the Taiwan format

S1.rule: a serving conversion is the printed mass or volume: (decimal text, canonical unit g or ml) of the first mass or volume printed in the truth's conversion, compared with the same of the candidate's; a truth conversion with no printed mass or volume (a count-only portion such as 2 sausages or 1 cracker) is not a conversion and leaves the denominator
S1.replaces: literal comparison of the conversion text with whitespace removed

M1.rule: an absolute value in a reference-intake column (8400kJ, 70g in an RI for an average adult column) is left out as unread with a warning, like *, instead of becoming a reference-intake cell that fails the whole candidate; it never counts as a missing amount

M2.rule: an energy value that prints no unit (704) takes the energy unit printed in its row label (Energy kJ) when the label prints exactly one energy unit, the value is a bare number, the column is not reference intake and the unit agrees with the row's nutrient; printed_text stays literal and a warning is recorded
M2.guard_note: the nutrient agreement check is a safety guard added in implementation: it can only leave a value unread, never attach a contradicting unit

M3.rule: a per-serving column with no printed serving line takes the mass or volume printed in its own header (per 30g serving, PER PACK (50g)) as its serving quantity, with a warning; a printed serving line still wins; the candidate's serving_size is never filled from a header
M3.review_fix: PR #259 review, 18 October 2026: the serving mass is read with S1's PRINTED_MASS pattern (a unit may not run on into a word), so '2 grilled sausages (90g)' gives 90g and '1 glass (250ml)' gives 250ml, never 2g or 1g; the serving-line parser (_serving_size) uses the same pattern.
